problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}{x}^{3}\,dx+z\,dy+y\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the helix $r(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,k$ for $t\in [0,\pi ]?$

activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Line Integrals With Respect to X and Y Over Parametric Curves

feedback.problem: Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}2y\,dx+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dy+3z\,dz,$ where $C$ is a portion of the curve $r(t)=\,i+t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ for $t\in [1,3]?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Along the curve, we have

$$
x(t)=1,\,y(t)=t,\,z(t)={t}^{2}.
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j+\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,k \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,k \\  & =\,j+2t\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}2y\,dx+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\,dy+3z\,dz & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,dt+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,dt+3z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(2y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}+3z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t})dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}2t\cdot (0)+\operatorname{ln}⁡1\cdot (1)+3{t}^{2}\cdot (2t)\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}6{t}^{2}\,dt\end{aligned}
$$
